title: You and Your Phone
text: Orientation week ends and the group chats begin: fourteen of them, all muted except the one that matters. Every Sunday your screen-time report lands like a parking ticket. Time to decide what kind of relationship you have with this rectangle.

ai.tone: playful, a little self-aware about phones
hints: This habit lasts until the online-presence choice at 36: say it quietly matters.
Never moralise; make the trade-off funny.

effects.text: You switch your screen to greyscale. Your thumb is confused but your evenings are back.

choices.label: Like everyone, about 2 h 20
choices.hint: The global average, give or take

effects.text: You scroll at exactly the speed of society.
Your first TikTac about the canteen gets 40,000 views. You check it 40,000 times.

title: The Asso Fair
text: The CentraleSupélec asso fair takes over the plateau: free crêpes, loud speakers, and forty people trying to recruit you in thirty seconds each. Everyone says your asso is your real degree. The ESSEC assos will court you next year in Cergy, if you can wait that long.

hints: Year 1, Saclay: only CentraleSupélec clubs recruit here. ESSEC assos recruit in Year 2, in Cergy, which is why waiting is an option.
The asso friend (Malik) is met here if the player joins any asso.

choices.label: Wait for the ESSEC fair
choices.hint: Cergy has the assos you came for

effects.text: You pocket three flyers and decide your asso life starts in Cergy. Year 1 is for surviving maths.

choices.label: No association
choices.hint: More sleep, more study, fewer stories

effects.text: You walk past the stands with the focus of someone who owns a library card.

title: A Sète Every Week
text: Year 2, Cergy. There is a sète every Thursday, and sometimes on Tuesday 'because it's someone's birthday'. Your grades, your liver and your friendships are negotiating a treaty. What kind of student are you this year?

variants.text: Year 2, Cergy. There is a sète every Thursday, and the person from that 3AM conversation keeps asking if you're coming. Your grades, your liver and your friendships are negotiating a treaty. What kind of student are you this year?

ai.tone: affectionate teasing, student slang (sète = party, ESSEC slang)
hints: This sets how often sète minis show up later in Year 2.

effects.text: Every bouncer at every sète knows your first name. Your 8AM self has filed a formal complaint.
You leave at 1AM, which everyone agrees is both wise and deeply suspicious.

choices.label: Library monk
choices.hint: Your grades thank you. Your friends?

effects.text: The library becomes your second home. The security guard knows your coffee order.

title: Summer Internship
text: Time for the mandatory three-month internship. Your LinkedOut feed is a wall of 'Thrilled to announce'. Your uncle still thinks AIDAMS is a brand of yoghurt. Where do you spend the summer?

hints: Locked options are greyed with their reason: acknowledge that assos and grades opened or closed doors.
This internship unlocks the Year 4 internship options.

choices.label: AI startup, twelve people
choices.lockedReason: Requires the AI club or Math & AI ≥ 35

effects.text: Day one: you push to production. Day two: you learn what 'rollback' means.
You format a pitch deck at 2AM and feel strangely alive. That should worry you.

choices.label: Impact NGO or social enterprise
choices.lockedReason: Requires the Impact asso or Impact ≥ 54

effects.text: You build a spreadsheet that actually helps people. It is the most beautiful spreadsheet in the world.

choices.label: Data analyst at a big corporate

effects.text: You discover the dashboard nobody reads. You make it beautiful. Nobody reads it.
Your model converges on a Friday at 6PM. Nobody is there to see it, so you tell the coffee machine.
